items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Your phone rings: "This is the F T C. Your number is linked to a crime." Would you stay on the line?
Narrator
The F T C warned about this exact call on October twenty-second.
Narrator
The caller says a phone in your name is running scams overseas. Cooperate, or your number gets deactivated.
Chars
[nervous, squeaky banknote, trembling] My number? I don't even have a phone.
Narrator
So why does a government call end with a payment?
Narrator
First, they pass you to a fake police officer. Then you're told you're under arrest.
Narrator
And then comes the part that costs you.
Narrator
To clear your name, you pay a "security deposit."
Narrator
That's the mirage: each step hands you to someone more official, so it feels more real.
Narrator
The F T C says real staff never ask for money, never threaten your phone, and never ask for secrecy.
Narrator
So the only thing to deactivate... is the call.
Narrator
Comment: has a fake agency ever called you?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
